correctness.rationale: Malikiosis applies because e^{-1} is transcendental. For the ambiguity sum, the exponent has two monotone branches with minima k^2 and (N-k)^2. Odd N gives a unique leading term, and the remaining weights total less than one fifth of it, proving the explicit nonzero margin. The standard Gabor criterion then gives phase retrieval. For even N, pairing j with j+N/2 at half-period shift gives equal weights and modulation ratio (-1)^ell, hence exact odd-ell cancellation.
correctness.risk: Even-dimensional zeros show failure of this sufficient certificate, not failure of phase retrieval itself.

value.rationale: The result identifies exact phase-retrieval behavior of a canonical earlier full-spark seed, including a quantitative odd-dimensional margin and a sharp even-dimensional cancellation mechanism.

final_claim: For \(\eta_N(j)=e^{-j^2}\), the finite Gabor orbit is full spark for every N; for odd \(N\ge3\) its self-ambiguity is zero-free with minimum at least \(\frac45e^{-(N-1)^2/4}\), hence yields phase retrieval, while for even N the ambiguity vanishes at half-period shift for every odd modulation.
limitations: The even-dimensional result is only an obstruction to the zero-free-ambiguity certificate.
